oneliner.t: Texas attorney general since 2015 and former state legislator who unseated Sen. John Cornyn in the May 26, 2026 Republican runoff (63.8% to 36.2%) after Trump endorsed him, and now faces Democrat James Talarico for the U.S. Senate.

born.t: December 23, 1962, Minot Air Force Base, Minot, North Dakota (born Warren Kenneth Paxton Jr.)

hometown.t: Raised in a moving Air Force family, mostly in California; graduated high school in Lawton, Oklahoma

upbringing.t: Paxton's father served in the U.S. Air Force, and the family of five lived in a trailer that moved with his postings, including Florida, New York, North Carolina, California and Oklahoma. He spent much of his childhood in California and graduated from MacArthur High School in Lawton, Oklahoma. He earned a psychology degree and an MBA at Baylor University, then a law degree at the University of Virginia. He married Angela Allen in 1986, and they have four children. Angela Paxton later became a Texas state senator. (These details come from one secondary source only.)

education.school: University of Virginia School of Law

career.role: Own law practice (estate planning, probate, real estate)
Attorney General of Texas (elected 2014, 2018, 2022; suspended May–Sept 2023 during impeachment)
career.org: Office of the Attorney General of Texas

platform.t: Ran as a senator who would support Trump on his priorities and 'stand up and fight for Republican values'; casts himself as an America First conservative. Trump endorsed him on May 19, 2026.
Deport criminal immigrants in the country illegally who, he says, entered under the Biden administration.
Cut taxes and stop wasteful spending.
Tied his decision to stay in the primary to a demand that the Senate end the filibuster to pass the SAVE America Act, a voter-citizenship bill.
End shipments of abortion pills into Texas.
Stand with Trump to protect gun rights.
As attorney general, defended Texas's anti-BDS law and reaffirmed it in October 2023. In August 2025 he opened an investigation into Plano ISD over alleged antisemitism and anti-Israel curriculum.

promises.t: Support President Trump's agenda in the Senate.
Deport criminal immigrants in the country illegally.
End the filibuster to pass the SAVE America Act.

record.t: PolitiFact rated it False. AFP Fact Check (cited by Media Bias/Fact Check) found Talarico is not vegan and has said publicly that he likes barbecue.

claims.claim: Campaign ad said Talarico wants the southern border to have 'a giant welcome mat out front.'

said.where: Paxton campaign TV ad (most-covered general-election ad found)

record.t: PolitiFact rated the ad Mostly False (2026-05-28). Talarico calls himself a 'border security Democrat' and backs the bipartisan Dignity Act, while also wanting ICE money redirected to other services.

claims.claim: Said he 'shut down the world's largest human trafficking marketplace.'

record.t: PolitiFact rated the claim Mostly False (2018-11-01). The full ruling was not opened for this review.

said.t: His campaign said in July that he would debate Talarico. Later that month it suggested a deal with a news outlet was close.

did.t: No debate had been scheduled as of Oct. 9. His campaign objected to some proposed moderators and did not respond publicly when Trump called for a debate on Oct. 7. Talarico had asked for three televised debates and later a Fox News debate.

entries.t: Politico reported in September 2026 that Paxton had not joined multistate efforts to regulate Kalshi, and that he and a supporting PAC had received donations from Kalshi and its CEO. His campaign declined to comment.

statements.t: Traveled to Israel with a National Association of Attorneys General delegation.
Reaffirmed Texas's law barring state contracts with companies that boycott Israel.
Opened an investigation into Plano ISD over alleged antisemitism and anti-Israel curriculum.
Backed Trump's strikes on Iran in the first week of the 2026 Iran war.

note.t: Not retrieved: his Senate candidate financial disclosure (Senate eFD) and his Texas Ethics Commission personal financial statements as attorney general were not reachable with this research tool. Separately, Cornyn's campaign alleged in 2025 that he claimed more than one property as his primary residence on bank loans. Paxton called that 'absolutely lying,' and no legal proceeding over it was found.

democracy.t: As attorney general, filed Texas v. Pennsylvania asking the U.S. Supreme Court to throw out the 62 electoral votes of Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin. The Court dismissed it on Dec. 11, 2020. Texas's solicitor general did not sign the filing.
Spoke at Trump's Jan. 6 rally before the Capitol attack and told the crowd 'we will not quit fighting.'
Tweeted that the people who stormed the Capitol were not Trump supporters and had been 'confirmed to be Antifa.' PolitiFact rated this Pants on Fire.

debates.note: No Republican primary or runoff debates were held, according to Wikipedia. In the general election, his campaign said in July it would debate, but none was scheduled as of Oct. 9, 2026, and no formal decline is on record.

note.t: Born in North Dakota and raised in a military family, mainly in California and Oklahoma. His documented ties to Texas begin with a Baylor degree in 1985 (a lower bound). He has held Texas public office since 2003.

checks.legal: CourtListener and Justia searches couldn't be run: this tool can only open URLs that appear in search results, so the 'courts' item is 'news'. Matters were compiled from Texas Tribune, AP (via Texas Tribune, NBC DFW and News 4 San Antonio), FOX 7, Denver Gazette, Texas Monthly, KSAT and Wikipedia: the 2015 state securities case (dismissed 2025-06-18), the SEC civil case (dismissed with prejudice 2017-03-02), the 2014 State Securities Board order, the 2023 impeachment and acquittal, the federal corruption probe (declined; reported 2025-04-03), the whistleblower judgment against his office, and the State Bar discipline suit (dismissed as moot Jan. 2025). Ethics: the State Bar matter came from news only. Texas Ethics Commission records were not searched. Also noted but not listed as legal matters: his wife's 2025 divorce filing (a family matter, no finding against him) and the mortgage/residence allegations (no proceeding found).

Financial disclosures (Senate eFD, Texas Ethics Commission) were not reachable, so foreign assets and income were not checked. News reviewed showed no foreign-government or foreign-business ties.

checks.democracy: Not in Congress, so no certification votes. Reviewed Wikipedia and PolitiFact for Texas v. Pennsylvania (2020), his Jan. 6, 2021 rally speech and his Jan. 7, 2021 tweet.

legal.t: A Collin County grand jury indicted him in 2015 on three felony securities-fraud counts. He was accused of soliciting investors for a Texas tech startup without disclosing that he was being paid in company stock, and he pleaded not guilty. In March 2024 he entered an 18-month pretrial intervention agreement with no plea and no admission of guilt. Under it he paid $271,000 in restitution, did more than 100 hours of community service and completed ethics training (30 hours, against 15 required). The charges were dismissed on June 18, 2025, in Harris County district court.
legal.status: Dismissed June 18, 2025 after he completed pretrial intervention; never convicted

legal.t: The Texas House impeached him 121–23 on May 27, 2023, on 20 articles alleging bribery and abuse of office, centered on favors for donor Nate Paul and the firing of whistleblowers. The Senate acquitted him on all 16 articles it tried on Sept. 16, 2023. No article got more than 14 of the 21 votes needed, and only two Republican senators voted to convict on any article. The Senate dismissed the other four articles, which concerned the securities case, by a 19–11 vote. His wife, Sen. Angela Paxton, was barred from voting.
legal.status: Acquitted Sept. 16, 2023; reinstated as attorney general

legal.t: Eight top aides reported him to the FBI in 2020, alleging bribery and abuse of office to help Nate Paul. A federal grand jury examined the matter, and the Justice Department's Public Integrity Section took it over in 2023. AP reported on 2025-04-03, citing anonymous sources, that DOJ decided in the final weeks of the Biden administration not to prosecute. A senior career official reportedly recommended against charges over doubts about winning a conviction, while the West Texas prosecutors who first handled the case reportedly believed the evidence supported an indictment. DOJ has not commented publicly.
legal.short: Federal corruption probe; no charges filed
legal.status: No federal charges ever filed. DOJ's decision not to prosecute is reported by AP sources, not officially announced

legal.t: The SEC filed a civil fraud suit in April 2016 over his solicitation of investors before he took office. On March 2, 2017, U.S. District Judge Amos Mazzant dismissed it with prejudice, finding he had no plausible legal duty to disclose his compensation arrangement.

Signed an agreed order with the Texas State Securities Board for acting as an investment adviser representative for Mowery Capital Management without registering. It carried a reprimand and a $1,000 fine.

Four former top deputies fired after reporting him to the FBI sued under the Texas Whistleblower Act in November 2020. In April 2025, Travis County District Judge Catherine Mauzy found the attorney general's office violated the act and awarded $6.6 million. Paxton dropped the office's appeal in July 2025. The judgment is against the agency, and Texas taxpayers pay it.
legal.status: Final judgment against the Office of the Attorney General after the appeal was dropped (July 2025); payment requires a legislative appropriation

legal.t: The State Bar's Commission for Lawyer Discipline sued him in May 2022, alleging he made false claims in the 2020 Texas v. Pennsylvania election suit. After the Texas Supreme Court threw out a parallel case against his deputy on separation-of-powers grounds (Dec. 2024), the bar dropped its case. The Supreme Court dismissed it as moot in January 2025.
legal.short: Bar discipline suit dropped, dismissed moot
legal.status: Dismissed as moot, January 2025, after voluntary dismissal; no ruling on the merits

recordx.note: Not in Congress, so there is no missed-vote figure. Disclosure timeliness (Senate eFD) and FEC notices (RFAI tab) could not be checked because those pages were not reachable with this tool.

corp.t: Donor-committee filings for 2025–26 show $88,000 from corporate PACs (among them ExxonMobil, Chevron, Valero, Halliburton, SpaceX, Altria, BNSF, Textron and U.S. Anesthesia Partners) and $30,000 from trade-association PACs (among them Wine & Spirits Wholesalers, IPAA Wildcatters, NSSF and DEPA). Politico also reported donations from Kalshi and its CEO to him and a supporting PAC.

lobby.t: NORPAC, a pro-Israel PAC, gave $1,000 (reported 2026-09-30). The Republican Jewish Coalition PAC, which some trackers count as pro-Israel, gave $5,000 (2026-06-01). No United Democracy Project spending was found in 2026 FEC independent-expenditure data.

research_notes: MONEY: FEC totals (S6TX00388, through 2026-09-30) and the committee-contribution and independent-expenditure files come from the FEC data already on disk. fec.gov pages, the FEC API, Track AIPAC and OpenSecrets could not be opened (provenance-restricted or blocked), so super PAC funders, the small- vs. large-donor split, industries and Track AIPAC career totals are missing. money_history is marked 'done' on the strength of direct FEC data only. Track AIPAC and super PAC donor checks still need a human. This was his first federal race, so 2026 is the only FEC cycle. The donor-reported PAC total ($302,032 + $62,000 NRSC) exceeds the candidate-reported $157,500, and the gap was not resolved. Outside spending: Texas PAC and No Going Back PAC report identical or near-identical sums as both supporting Paxton and opposing Talarico, which is likely the same ads coded twice, so don't add them. AdImpact says more than $247M has been spent on ads in the race overall. LEGAL: the impeachment, securities, SEC, federal-probe, whistleblower and bar outcomes are documented above with exact status. Sources differ on the 2015 indictment date (July per Denver Gazette; August per Texas Tribune, likely when it was unsealed). PERSONAL: his wife Angela filed for divorce in 2025 on 'biblical grounds' (Fox News). This is a family-court matter with no finding, so it is not listed as a legal item. Alleged extramarital conduct was part of the impeachment articles, on which he was acquitted. NOT FOUND: campaign website URL, campaign bio and issues pages, Senate eFD report, Texas Ethics Commission filings, FEC RFAI status, photo. CLAIMS: only 3 checkable claims could be sourced. Needs a human pass on the campaign site.
